steps.name: environment
steps.description: Ensure workspace exists, persist STREAMLIT headless environment both globally (/etc/profile.d) and locally ($WS/.env_streamlit) atomically, validate sudo availability, and verify pip3 presence. Writing the workspace-local env guarantees non-login shells can source it; writing /etc/profile.d provides future shell sessions the variables. Validate syntax by sourcing in a subshell after write.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WS="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/streamlit-tic-tac-toe-255584-255684/tic_tac_toe_native_app"
sudo --version >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
mkdir -p "$WS" && cd "$WS"
# workspace-local env (always created/updated)
LOCAL_ENV="$WS/.env_streamlit"
TMP="/tmp/env_streamlit.$$"
cat > "$TMP" <<'EOF'
# Streamlit headless environment (workspace-local)
export STREAMLIT_SERVER_HEADLESS=true
export STREAMLIT_SERVER_RUN_ON_SAVE=false
EOF
mv "$TMP" "$LOCAL_ENV" && chmod 644 "$LOCAL_ENV"
# global env in /etc/profile.d if sudo available
if command -v sudo >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  GLOBAL=/etc/profile.d/streamlit_env.sh
  TMP2="/tmp/streamlit_env.$$"
  cat > "$TMP2" <<'EOF'
# Streamlit headless environment (managed by setup script)
export STREAMLIT_SERVER_HEADLESS=true
export STREAMLIT_SERVER_RUN_ON_SAVE=false
EOF
  if [ -f "$GLOBAL" ]; then
    if sudo cmp -s "$TMP2" "$GLOBAL"; then rm -f "$TMP2"; else sudo mv "$TMP2" "$GLOBAL" && sudo chmod 644 "$GLOBAL"; fi
  else
    sudo mv "$TMP2" "$GLOBAL" && sudo chmod 644 "$GLOBAL"
  fi
  # quick syntax check by sourcing in a subshell
  sudo bash -c "source $GLOBAL" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
fi
# Verify pip3 present
if ! command -v pip3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "pip3 not found" >&2
  exit 2
fi
pip3 --version >/dev/null 2>&1

steps.name: project scaffolding
steps.description: Create minimal Streamlit project files (import-safe app.py), static directory, requirements.txt placeholder, workspace-local env file is already created by env-001, and a robust start script (start_streamlit.sh) that launches streamlit from the workspace venv when present, redirects logs to $WS/streamlit.log, writes the actual server PID atomically, sets its own process group (via setsid) and cleans up pidfile on exit. Files are only created if missing to preserve developer content.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WS="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/streamlit-tic-tac-toe-255584-255684/tic_tac_toe_native_app"
mkdir -p "$WS" && cd "$WS"
# import-safe app.py (avoid top-level Streamlit side-effects except imports)
if [ ! -f "$WS/app.py" ]; then
  cat > "$WS/app.py" <<'PY'
try:
    import streamlit as st
except Exception:
    # keep import-time failures visible during test/install but avoid crashing tools
    st = None

def app():
    if not st:
        raise RuntimeError('streamlit not available')
    st.title('Tic Tac Toe (dev container stub)')
    st.write('This is a minimal scaffold for local development.')

if __name__ == '__main__':
    app()
PY
fi
mkdir -p "$WS/static"
if [ ! -f "$WS/requirements.txt" ]; then
  cat > "$WS/requirements.txt" <<'REQ'
streamlit
pytest
REQ
fi
# robust start script
if [ ! -f "$WS/start_streamlit.sh" ]; then
  cat > "$WS/start_streamlit.sh" <<'SH'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WS="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
# source workspace-local env then global if present
[ -f "$WS/.env_streamlit" ] && source "$WS/.env_streamlit" || true
[ -f /etc/profile.d/streamlit_env.sh ] && source /etc/profile.d/streamlit_env.sh || true
LOG="$WS/streamlit.log"
PIDFILE="$WS/streamlit.pid"
VENV="$WS/.venv"
# cleanup stale pidfile
if [ -f "$PIDFILE" ]; then
  PID=$(cat "$PIDFILE" 2>/dev/null || true)
  if [ -n "$PID" ] && ps -p "$PID" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "streamlit already running (PID $PID)" >&2
    exit 1
  else
    rm -f "$PIDFILE"
  fi
fi
# choose python/streamlit binary
if [ -x "$VENV/bin/streamlit" ]; then
  STREAMLIT_EXEC="$VENV/bin/streamlit"
else
  STREAMLIT_EXEC="$(command -v streamlit || true)"
fi
if [ -z "$STREAMLIT_EXEC" ]; then
  echo "streamlit not found in PATH or venv" >&2
  exit 2
fi
# start under new session so we can kill group reliably; redirect logs
setsid "$STREAMLIT_EXEC" run "$WS/app.py" --server.port=8501 --server.address=0.0.0.0 >"$LOG" 2>&1 &
CHILD=$!
# write pid atomically
TMPPID="${PIDFILE}.tmp.$$"
echo "$CHILD" > "$TMPPID" && mv "$TMPPID" "$PIDFILE"
# trap to cleanup pidfile on exit
trap 'rm -f "$PIDFILE" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true' EXIT
wait $CHILD
SH
  chmod +x "$WS/start_streamlit.sh"
fi

steps.name: install dependencies
steps.description: Always create a deterministic workspace virtualenv (.venv) and install requirements into it non-interactively. Write pip logs to pip-install.log. Expose venv binaries by explicit use in subsequent steps; do NOT modify global site-packages. Verify imports using the venv python to ensure later steps run successfully.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WS="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/streamlit-tic-tac-toe-255584-255684/tic_tac_toe_native_app"
cd "$WS"
VENV="$WS/.venv"
PIP_LOG="$WS/pip-install.log"
REQ="$WS/requirements.txt"
python3 -m venv "$VENV"
# ensure pip in venv is upgraded quietly
"$VENV/bin/python" -m pip install --upgrade pip >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
# install requirements (require non-empty file)
if [ -f "$REQ" ] && [ -s "$REQ" ]; then
  "$VENV/bin/pip" install --no-input --disable-pip-version-check --no-cache-dir -r "$REQ" >"$PIP_LOG" 2>&1
else
  "$VENV/bin/pip" install --no-input --disable-pip-version-check --no-cache-dir streamlit pytest >"$PIP_LOG" 2>&1
fi
# verify imports using venv python
"$VENV/bin/python" - <<'PY'
import sys
try:
    import streamlit, pytest
except Exception as e:
    print('dependency-import-failure:', e, file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(4)
print('ok')
PY

steps.name: validation
steps.description: Start the Streamlit app using start_streamlit.sh (which uses venv when present), wait for HTTP responsiveness on port 8501, capture evidence (HTTP root snippet and last lines of streamlit.log), then terminate the server reliably by killing its process group. Handle stale pidfile before start and ensure cleanup after stop. Use robust port checks with ss fallback to grep.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WS="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/streamlit-tic-tac-toe-255584-255684/tic_tac_toe_native_app"
cd "$WS"
LOG="$WS/streamlit.log"
PIDFILE="$WS/streamlit.pid"
# source envs
[ -f "$WS/.env_streamlit" ] && source "$WS/.env_streamlit" || true
[ -f /etc/profile.d/streamlit_env.sh ] && source /etc/profile.d/streamlit_env.sh || true
# stale pidfile cleanup
if [ -f "$PIDFILE" ]; then
  PID=$(cat "$PIDFILE" 2>/dev/null || true)
  if [ -z "$PID" ] || ! ps -p "$PID" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    rm -f "$PIDFILE"
  else
    echo "port 8501 appears in use by PID $PID; aborting validation" >&2
    exit 5
  fi
fi
# check port in use (ss fallback grep)
if ss -ltn | grep -q ':8501' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "port 8501 appears in use; aborting validation" >&2
  exit 5
fi
# start helper that runs start_streamlit.sh (it writes pidfile and log)
./start_streamlit.sh &
START_HELPER_PID=$!
# wait for pidfile
ATTEMPTS=30
OK=0
for i in $(seq 1 $ATTEMPTS); do
  if [ -f "$PIDFILE" ] && [ -s "$PIDFILE" ]; then
    PID=$(cat "$PIDFILE" | tr -d ' ')
    if ps -p "$PID" >/dev/null 2>&1; then OK=1 && break; fi
  fi
  sleep 1
done
if [ "$OK" -ne 1 ]; then
  echo "Streamlit pidfile not created or process not running. Tail of log:" >&2
  tail -n 200 "$LOG" >&2 || true
  kill "$START_HELPER_PID" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  exit 3
fi
# obtain PGID and wait for HTTP readiness
PGID=$(ps -o pgid= "$PID" | tr -d ' ' || true)
ATTEMPTS=60
OK=0
for i in $(seq 1 $ATTEMPTS); do
  if curl -sSf --max-time 3 http://127.0.0.1:8501/ >/dev/null 2>&1 || curl -sSf --max-time 3 http://[::1]:8501/ >/dev/null 2>&1 || curl -sSf --max-time 3 http://localhost:8501/ >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    OK=1 && break
  fi
  sleep 1
done
if [ "$OK" -ne 1 ]; then
  echo "Streamlit did not respond within timeout. Tail of log:" >&2
  tail -n 200 "$LOG" >&2 || true
  # attempt group kill
  if [ -n "$PGID" ]; then kill -TERM -"$PGID" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; fi
  kill "$PID" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  exit 4
fi
# evidence: small HTTP snippet and tail of log
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8501/ | head -c 200 || true
echo
echo "--- streamlit.log tail ---"
tail -n 50 "$LOG" || true
echo "PID=$PID PGID=$PGID"
# stop server: kill process group if available, else PID
if [ -n "$PGID" ]; then
  kill -TERM -"$PGID" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
else
  kill "$PID" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
fi
sleep 1
# ensure helper process stopped
kill "$START_HELPER_PID" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
rm -f "$PIDFILE"
echo "validation: success"

    if ps -p "$PID" >/dev/null 2>&1; then OK=1 && break; fi
  fi
  sleep 1
done
if [ "$OK" -ne 1 ]; then
  echo "Streamlit pidfile not created or process not running. Tail of log:" >&2
  tail -n 200 "$LOG" >&2 || true
  kill "$START_HELPER_PID" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  exit 3
fi
# obtain PGID and wait for HTTP readiness
PGID=$(ps -o pgid= "$PID" | tr -d ' ' || true)
ATTEMPTS=60
OK=0
for i in $(seq 1 $ATTEMPTS); do
  if curl -sSf --max-time 3 http://127.0.0.1:8501/ >/dev/null 2>&1 || curl -sSf --max-time 3 http://[::1]:8501/ >/dev/null 2>&1 || curl -sSf --max-time 3 http://localhost:8501/ >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    OK=1 && break
  fi
  sleep 1
done
if [ "$OK" -ne 1 ]; then
  echo "Streamlit did not respond within timeout. Tail of log:" >&2
  tail -n 200 "$LOG" >&2 || true
  # attempt group kill
  if [ -n "$PGID" ]; then kill -TERM -"$PGID" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; fi
  kill "$PID" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  exit 4
fi
# evidence: small HTTP snippet and tail of log
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8501/ | head -c 200 || true
echo
echo "--- streamlit.log tail ---"
tail -n 50 "$LOG" || true
echo "PID=$PID PGID=$PGID"
# stop server: kill process group if available, else PID
if [ -n "$PGID" ]; then
  kill -TERM -"$PGID" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
else
  kill "$PID" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
fi
sleep 1
# ensure helper process stopped
kill "$START_HELPER_PID" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
rm -f "$PIDFILE"
echo "validation: success"

reasoning: Apply analyst recommendations prioritizing correctness and deterministic behavior in a headless container. Tests and validation explicitly call $WS/.venv/bin/pytest and $WS/.venv/bin/python so they run in the same environment. Scripts follow required shebang, strict error handling, use the authoritative workspace path, and minimize interactive prompts. These changes address all HIGH-level recommendations (always use venv, ensure venv visibility, reliable PID/PGID handling, robust start/stop and stale-pid handling, safer env persistence) and several MEDIUM/LOW suggestions (robust port checks, consolidated detection, atomic pid writes, workspace-local env file, log redirection).
